title: Advice to young drummers
summary: He tells young drummers to learn their instrument, learn to read and always arrive early.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Uh huh. Is there anything you would like to say in conclusion; something you would like to advise young musicians or young drummers -- what would you tell them, since this is part of your story. To wind up this thing, what advice would you give a young musician, and especially, a young drummer?

Well, I would like to tell young drummers that, since they have the opportunities that I didn't have, to try and learn as much as they can about their instrument; try and learn the drum well and if they can, try to learn how to play a little vibes, a little temp; but of all

things, go and learn how to read, how to make time -- if the man says, or whoever you work for, says to be there at eight o'clock, try to be there at a quarter of eight with your drums set up, so when eight o'clock comes, you'll be ready to hit.
